bacterial_leaf_blight.name: Bacterial Leaf Blight
symptoms: Water-soaked yellowish stripes on leaf margins
Leaves turn yellow-white and dry up from the tip downward
Milky or opaque bacterial ooze on young lesions in the morning
causes: Bacterium Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae
High humidity, heavy rain, and strong winds
Excessive nitrogen fertilizer application
organic_controls: Drain standing water from the field for 3-4 days to halt bacterial spread
Spray fresh cow dung slurry (20 g/L filtered) or Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/L as preventive bio-control
treatments: Apply copper-based bactericide ONLY if spread >10%: Copper oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L + Streptocycline @ 0.1 g/L
Avoid spraying during strong winds or rain
do_not_do: Do NOT apply extra urea/nitrogen fertilizer—it accelerates bacterial blight
Do NOT use fungal sprays or unverified cocktail mixtures from local shops; fungicides do not kill bacteria
preventions: Use resistant paddy varieties (e.g., Improved Samba Mahsuri)
Apply balanced nitrogen fertilizer in split doses
Treat seeds with Streptocycline before sowing

brown_spot.name: Brown Spot
symptoms: Oval or circular brown spots with a yellow halo on leaves
Spots may coalesce and cause leaves to wither
Dark brown discoloration on rice grains
causes: Fungus Bipolaris oryzae
Nutrient-deficient or poorly drained soils
High humidity and warm temperatures (25-30 C)
organic_controls: Correct potassium/zinc soil deficiency first—Brown Spot is strongly linked to poor soil nutrition
Spray Trichoderma viride or Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/L at early symptom stage
treatments: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2 g/L or Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1 g/L only if spots cover >5-10% leaf area
Correct soil potassium and silicon deficiencies
do_not_do: Do NOT spray antibiotics or insecticides for Brown Spot (it is fungal + nutritional)
Do NOT exceed recommended label dosage
preventions: Use certified, disease-free seeds
Apply balanced NPK fertilizers
Maintain proper field drainage

leaf_smut.name: Leaf Smut
symptoms: Small, slightly raised black linear spots on both sides of leaves
Leaves may turn yellow and senesce prematurely in severe cases
causes: Fungus Entyloma oryzae
High nitrogen levels and late-season humidity
organic_controls: Remove heavily spotted lower leaves manually and maintain clean bunds
Skip chemical spraying in mild cases—Leaf Smut rarely reduces yield on its own
treatments: Usually minor; apply Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1 mL/L ONLY if widespread across upper flag leaves
do_not_do: Do NOT buy expensive broad-spectrum chemical cocktails for minor Leaf Smut
preventions: Avoid excessive nitrogen application
Practice clean field sanitation and compost infected stubble after harvest

blast.name: Rice Blast
symptoms: Diamond-shaped or spindle-shaped lesions with gray centers and brown margins
Neck rot causing panicles to break or turn white (chaffy grains)
Rapid drying of foliage in severe infections
causes: Fungus Magnaporthe oryzae
Cool nights, high humidity, and prolonged leaf wetness
Excessive nitrogen fertilization
organic_controls: Maintain shallow flooding (avoid drying/cracking stress) and stop nitrogen top-dressing immediately
Preventive spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/L during tillering
treatments: Spray Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6 g/L or Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5 mL/L
Repeat spray after 10-12 days ONLY if active lesions persist
do_not_do: Do NOT spray in strong midday heat or before heavy rain
Do NOT mix multiple unverified fungicides together
preventions: Plant blast-resistant rice varieties
Avoid dense planting and excessive nitrogen
Remove infected crop residues after harvest

tungro.name: Rice Tungro Virus
symptoms: Yellow-orange discoloration starting from leaf tips
Stunted plant growth and reduced tillering
Delayed flowering and incomplete panicle exertion
causes: Rice tungro bacilliform and spherical viruses
Transmitted by Green Leafhopper (Nephotettix virescens)
organic_controls: Uproot and bury infected plants early before leafhoppers spread the virus
Install yellow sticky traps (8-10/acre) to monitor Green Leafhoppers
treatments: Control green leafhopper vectors using Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.3 mL/L only when hopper threshold is exceeded
do_not_do: Do NOT spray fungicides—Tungro is a viral disease and fungicides have zero effect
preventions: Practice synchronous planting across neighboring fields
Use tungro-resistant varieties
Keep bunds free of grassy weeds

normal.name: Healthy Paddy Leaf
symptoms: Uniform vibrant green leaf blade with no lesions or spots
Healthy tillering and upright leaf posture
causes: Optimal water, nutrient, and pest management
organic_controls: Continue balanced organic/compost nutrition and natural predator conservation
treatments: No chemical treatment required
do_not_do: Do NOT apply preventive chemical pesticides on a healthy crop
preventions: Continue regular field monitoring twice a week
Maintain balanced irrigation and fertilization

tomato_early_blight.name: Tomato Early Blight
symptoms: Dark brown circular spots with concentric 'target-board' rings on older lower leaves
Yellowing halo around lesions leading to premature leaf drop
causes: Fungus Alternaria solani
Warm humid weather and overhead irrigation splashing soil onto lower leaves
organic_controls: Prune and destroy infected lower leaves; mulch soil to prevent rain splash
Spray Trichoderma viride @ 5 g/L or Neem oil (1500 ppm) @ 3 mL/L
treatments: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2 g/L or Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2 g/L at 7-10 day intervals
do_not_do: Do NOT use overhead sprinklers in the evening
Do NOT mix multiple copper and sulfur sprays without label guidance
preventions: Rotate tomato with non-solanaceous crops (cereals/legumes) for 2-3 years
Stake plants for better airflow

tomato_late_blight.name: Tomato Late Blight
symptoms: Irregular water-soaked greenish-black patches on leaves and stems
White cottony fungal growth on leaf undersides during cool humid mornings
causes: Oomycete Phytophthora infestans
Cool, cloudy, wet weather (>85% humidity)
organic_controls: Immediately remove and bury severely infected plants to protect neighboring rows
Avoid dense canopy and improve field drainage
treatments: Spray Metalaxyl + Mancozeb (Ridomil Gold) @ 2 g/L or Cymoxanil + Mancozeb @ 2 g/L
do_not_do: Do NOT wait if cool wet weather persists—Late Blight can destroy a plot in days
Do NOT compost blighted vines near the field
preventions: Plant certified disease-free seedlings
Avoid planting near infected potato fields

tomato_bacterial_spot.name: Tomato Bacterial Spot
symptoms: Small, dark, water-soaked greasy spots on leaves and green fruits
Leaves turn yellow and drop, exposing fruits to sunscald
causes: Xanthomonas spp. bacteria spread by wind-driven rain and infected seeds
organic_controls: Avoid working in the field when foliage is wet
Remove severely spotted lower leaves
treatments: Spray Copper oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L + Streptocycline @ 0.1 g/L
do_not_do: Do NOT spray standard fungicides—they do not control bacterial spot
preventions: Use hot-water or Streptocycline-treated seeds
Follow 2-year crop rotation

tomato_tomato_yellowleaf_curl_virus.name: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus (TYLCV)
symptoms: Upward curling and cupping of young leaves with yellow margins
Severe stunting and flower drop
causes: Begomovirus transmitted by Whitefly (Bemisia tabaci)
organic_controls: Rogue out infected plants early and install yellow sticky traps (10/acre)
Spray Neem oil (1500 ppm) @ 3 mL/L to deter whiteflies
treatments: Manage whitefly vectors using Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.3 mL/L or Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.2 g/L
do_not_do: Do NOT spray fungicides—TYLCV is a viral disease
preventions: Use insect-proof net nurseries and TYLCV-resistant hybrids

potato_early_blight.name: Potato Early Blight
symptoms: Brown-black lesions with concentric rings on older leaves
Premature defoliation reducing tuber size
causes: Fungus Alternaria solani favored by warm alternating wet/dry weather
organic_controls: Maintain adequate nitrogen and potassium nutrition
Spray Trichoderma viride @ 5 g/L preventively
treatments: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2 g/L or Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1 mL/L
do_not_do: Do NOT under-fertilize—stressed potato plants suffer worse Early Blight
preventions: Use healthy seed tubers and 3-year crop rotation

potato_late_blight.name: Potato Late Blight
symptoms: Water-soaked dark lesions on leaf tips/margins with white mold underneath
Rapid stem rot and tuber brown rot
causes: Oomycete Phytophthora infestans in cool, humid, foggy weather
organic_controls: Hill up soil around tubers to block spore wash-down
Destroy volunteer potato plants
treatments: Spray Cymoxanil + Mancozeb @ 2 g/L or Dimethomorph + Mancozeb @ 2 g/L
do_not_do: Do NOT harvest tubers while blighted foliage is still green and wet
preventions: Plant certified blight-free seed tubers and resistant varieties

pepper_bell_bacterial_spot.name: Chilli / Pepper Bacterial Spot
symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves turning dark brown with yellow halos
Raised corky spots on pods
causes: Xanthomonas campestris pv. vesicatoria spread by rain splash
organic_controls: Avoid overhead watering and prune heavily infected leaves
treatments: Spray Copper hydroxide or Copper oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L
do_not_do: Do NOT use fungicides alone for bacterial spot
preventions: Use disease-free seeds and 2-3 year rotation

corn_maize_common_rust.name: Maize Common Rust
symptoms: Small cinnamon-brown powdery pustules on both upper and lower leaf surfaces
causes: Fungus Puccinia sorghi favored by cool, humid nights (16-23 C)
organic_controls: Grow resistant maize hybrids; mild rust rarely needs chemical spray
treatments: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2 g/L or Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1 mL/L if severe before tasseling
do_not_do: Do NOT spray late after grain-filling is complete
preventions: Select rust-resistant hybrids and avoid late planting

apple_apple_scab.name: Apple Scab
symptoms: Olive-green to dark velvety spots on leaves and scabby lesions on fruit
causes: Fungus Venturia inaequalis overwintering in fallen leaves
organic_controls: Rake and compost/burn fallen leaves in autumn to break the cycle
treatments: Spray Captan 50% WP @ 2 g/L or Dodine 65% WP @ 1 g/L at green-tip/petal-fall
do_not_do: Do NOT leave infected leaf litter under trees
preventions: Prune canopy for airflow and plant scab-resistant cultivars

grape_black_rot.name: Grape Black Rot
symptoms: Reddish-brown leaf spots with black fruiting bodies; shriveled black 'mummy' berries
causes: Fungus Guignardia bidwellii in warm, wet spring/summer weather
organic_controls: Remove mummified berries and prune canes for sun/air penetration
treatments: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2 g/L or Myclobutanil 10% WP @ 0.4 g/L
do_not_do: Do NOT leave mummified clusters hanging on vines
preventions: Sanitize vineyard floor and train vines on open trellises

apple_black_rot.name: Apple — Black Rot
symptoms: Visible black rot lesions, discoloration, or damage on apple foliage.
causes: Pathogen or pest pressure associated with black rot under favorable humidity/temperature.
organic_controls: Prune and destroy heavily infected leaves away from the field.
Apply Neem oil (3-5 mL/L) or Trichoderma/Pseudomonas bio-control as early intervention.
treatments: Consult local KVK or agri-extension officer for targeted black rot control if spread exceeds 10%.
Ensure proper field drainage and avoid overhead irrigation.
do_not_do: Do NOT mix unverified chemical cocktails.
Do NOT over-apply nitrogen fertilizer during active infection.
preventions: Use certified disease-free seeds or resistant varieties.
Practice crop rotation and maintain proper plant spacing.
